propositions: For a text containing exactly one JSON object, _candidate_dicts appends the same decoded dict twice—once from _all_json_objects and once from json.loads—causing false multiple-candidate warnings.

The ambiguity detection logic uses identity comparison (is not) on separately constructed Pydantic instances, which returns true even when the instances are semantically equal, triggering spurious conflict warnings.
Deduplicating semantically identical decoded dicts in discovery order before validation prevents false ambiguity warnings while preserving last-valid-wins behavior for genuinely distinct candidates.
Native structured replies that contain a single valid JSON object should emit no multiple-candidate warning and yield one candidate.
